 Thanksgiving food prices: What’s costing more and how shoppers can save
 18-Nov-2026 at 12:50 PM EST ,
 by Tulane University 
 ♡ 
 Credit: Pexels 
 Thanksgiving dinner will cost more this year, but shoppers may find some surprising bargains. While wholesale turkey prices are up 8% and fresh cranberries and several vegetables have climbed more than 10%, grocery store discounts could help keep the holiday meal affordable. With overall food prices up about 2.5%, a traditional Thanksgiving dinner for 10 is expected to cost between $55 and $80, excluding beverages.
 Tulane University expert Mark Ratchford is available to explain why higher turkey prices don’t necessarily mean bigger grocery bills, which holiday staples are seeing the steepest increases and how families can save by using store promotions, meal bundles and simple substitutions.
 For interviews, contact Roger Dunaway at  [email protected] or 504-452-2906.
